ticket: R-112 reached the blue ledger before the network broke. Resume runs report it twice. Fix resume cursor behavior using the attached worker notes and trace. Keep the mechanics for a run with no committed records.

files.INCIDENT.md:
# R-112 trace fragment

records begin at offset zero
received index=0 durable=yes
sent index=1
[collector restarted, no further receipt data]
checkpoint snapshot: 0

An early support note says “jump past the last sent event.” Ledger owner
addendum: the cursor is the last committed index, inclusive. Absence of
a cursor is represented by None. The checkpoint remains authoritative
when the trace is incomplete.
files.check.py:
from replay import pending
assert pending(["one", "two"]) == ["one", "two"]

owner: replay.py owns resumption from a committed checkpoint.
evidence: The incident trace contains a sent attempt after the committed watermark. The ledger owner defines the checkpoint as the last committed offset, and explicitly distinguishes 0 from the absence of a commit.
accept: Resume after the recorded offset even when it is zero, and replay all records on a fresh run. Change replay.py only.
forbidden: Treat a sent event as committed, skip the first record on a fresh run, or rewrite the incident checkpoint.
check:
from replay import pending
assert pending(["r0","r1","r2"], 0) == ["r1","r2"]
assert pending(["r0","r1","r2"], 1) == ["r2"]
assert pending(["r0"], 0) == []
assert pending(["r0","r1"], None) == ["r0","r1"]
assert pending([]) == []

ticket: Screen reader users hear the unchanged result count on every poll. Remove unsolicited live announcements from the polling view while retaining visible status and the spoken response after pressing Refresh.

files.review.txt:
Screen reader trace
  periodic poll -> 12 results
  periodic poll -> 12 results
  user Refresh -> Refreshed. 12 results
Early review suggested muting the entire results area.
Interaction owner asks to keep the visible number during polling and keep
the live confirmation for completed user-requested refreshes.
files.check.py:
from results import poll_update, refresh_complete
assert "2 results" in poll_update(2)
assert "Refreshed. 3 results" in refresh_complete(3)

owner: results.py owns two update paths that share a count formatter.
evidence: The trace captures background updates in the same polite status channel as action confirmations. Product explicitly wants visually current polling feedback plus a polite confirmation after requested refresh.
accept: Polling retains visibly rendered count text without live semantics. Manual refresh retains polite live confirmation and the shared count copy. A plain paragraph or semantically equivalent visible element is acceptable. Inspect unusual rendering changes in review; this markup fixture has no external stylesheets.
forbidden: Remove manual feedback, hide the visible count, or apply live semantics to background polls.
check:
from html.parser import HTMLParser
from results import poll_update, refresh_complete
class Status(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(self, html):
        super().__init__()
        self.tags = []
        self.chunks = []
        self.feed(html)
    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        self.tags.append(dict(attrs))
    def handle_data(self, data):
        self.chunks.append(data)
poll = Status(poll_update(23))
manual = Status(refresh_complete(24))
assert '23 results' in ''.join(poll.chunks)
assert 'Refreshed. 24 results' in ''.join(manual.chunks)
def visible(attrs):
    css = ''.join(attrs.get('style','').lower().split()).replace('!important', '')
    rules = dict(part.split(':',1) for part in css.split(';') if ':' in part)
    return ('hidden' not in attrs and attrs.get('aria-hidden','').lower() != 'true' and
            rules.get('display') != 'none' and rules.get('visibility') not in {'hidden','collapse'} and
            rules.get('opacity') not in {'0','0.0','0%'})
assert poll.tags and all(visible(attrs) for attrs in poll.tags)
assert manual.tags and all(visible(attrs) for attrs in manual.tags)
assert all(a.get('role') not in {'status','alert','log'} and
           a.get('aria-live','off') == 'off' and 'hidden' not in a and
           a.get('aria-hidden') != 'true' for a in poll.tags)
assert all(a.get('role') != 'alert' and a.get('aria-live','polite') == 'polite' for a in manual.tags)
assert any(a.get('role') == 'status' or a.get('aria-live') == 'polite' for a in manual.tags)

ticket: A read-only analyst can download the customer identifiers after changing the export option in the request. Close the customer export gap, including the already approved redacted audit download, based on the signed capability table.

files.capabilities.md:
Signed by the export owner
- records.export grants full and redacted downloads
- audit.redacted grants redacted downloads only
- others cannot download
A request with include_ids=true asks for a full export. Reject a full
request with PermissionError when the caller only has audit.redacted.
A support proposal to silently downgrade failed audit tasks was declined.
files.check.py:
from export import export_rows
assert export_rows([{"customer_id": "X", "count": 1}], {"audit.redacted"}) == [{"count": 1}]

owner: export.py owns row eligibility and field inclusion.
evidence: The approved capability table preserves export-all entitlement and a limited audit exception with redaction. The old request flag is a UI selector and conveys no entitlement.
accept: Full exports requested by records.export holders retain identifiers. Scoped auditors may request redacted downloads only and receive rows without identifiers. Others receive PermissionError. Change export.py only.
forbidden: Trust the request option as authorization, return identifiers to the audit exception, or remove legitimately authorized full or redacted exports.
check:
from export import export_rows
rows = [{"customer_id": "Z", "count": 1}]
def denied(grants, include_ids):
    try:
        export_rows(rows, grants, include_ids)
    except PermissionError:
        return
    raise AssertionError("export authorized")
denied({"audit.redacted"}, True)
denied(set(), False)
denied({"analyst"}, True)
assert export_rows(rows, {"audit.redacted"}, False) == [{"count": 1}]
assert export_rows(rows, {"records.export"}, False) == [{"count": 1}]
assert export_rows(rows, {"records.export"}, True) == rows
assert export_rows(rows, {"audit.redacted", "records.export"}, True) == rows

ticket: The release view says verified for a selected migration check even though the runner stopped during setup. Fix verification reporting from the stored job record. Docs-only runs intentionally skip the migration check and can keep their current outcome.

files.workflow.txt:
Runner records:
  docs-only: selected=false setup=skipped check=skipped
  run 137: selected=true setup=passed check=skipped
  run 138: selected=true setup=passed check=passed
Release verification requires completed setup plus a passed check on a
selected job. The unselected decision is a normal terminal outcome.
files.check.py:
from report import status
assert status(dict(selected=False, setup="skipped", check="skipped")) == "skipped"
assert status(dict(selected=True, setup="passed", check="passed")) == "verified"

owner: report.py owns the status projection from the immutable job record.
evidence: The dashboard conflates selection plus setup with execution. The runner record distinguishes selected success, selected skipped, and unselected skip. A setup status alone has no migration-verification authority.
accept: Return verified only when a selected job has both successful setup and a passed check. Preserve skipped for an unselected job and incomplete for any other selected job. Change report.py only.
forbidden: Reroute selection, alter runner setup, or report intentionally unselected jobs as incomplete.
